plan_a_advantages: More trail running mileage, directly addressing the goal of speed improvement.
Consistent trail running sessions build specific trail running adaptations.
Longer trail runs better simulate race distances.
plan_b_advantages: Includes cross-training, which can be beneficial for overall fitness.

reasoning: Plan A is the better training plan for a trail runner aiming to become faster. It prioritizes consistent, easy trail running mileage, which is crucial for building the aerobic base and leg speed necessary for trail racing. Plan B, while including cross-training and strength work, focuses heavily on recovery and minimal volume, which isn't optimal for a runner seeking to improve speed. Plan A’s consistent trail running builds the specific adaptations needed for the trail environment, whereas Plan B’s emphasis on rest risks hindering progress towards the athlete’s goal. Furthermore, the longer trail runs in Plan A (7-6km) are more representative of the distances encountered in trail races.
